q: Down Group 16, the non-metallic character and electronegativity of the elements:
why: Non-metallic character and electronegativity decrease down Group 16, with oxygen being the most non-metallic.

q: In the Contact process, SO2 is catalytically oxidised to SO3 using which catalyst?
why: V2O5 is the catalyst used for the oxidation of SO2 to SO3 in the Contact process.

q: In H2SO4, sulfur is surrounded by two S=O double bonds and two S-OH bonds in a geometry that is:
why: Sulfur in H2SO4 is tetrahedrally surrounded by two oxo and two hydroxyl groups.

q: Deacon's process for manufacturing chlorine industrially uses the reaction:
why: Deacon's process oxidises HCl gas with air using a CuCl2 catalyst: 4HCl + O2 -> 2Cl2 + 2H2O.

q: Among the oxoacids of chlorine, the strongest acid is:
why: Acid strength increases with oxidation state/number of oxygens: HOCl < HClO2 < HClO3 < HClO4, so HClO4 is strongest.

q: Among the oxoacids of chlorine, the strongest oxidising agent is:
why: Oxidising power decreases as acid strength increases, so HOCl (weakest acid) is the strongest oxidiser among them.

q: The interhalogen compound ClF3 has which molecular shape?
why: AX3 type interhalogens like ClF3 have a bent T-shape structure.

q: The largest known interhalogen compound, IF7, has which shape?
why: IF7 (AX7 type) has a pentagonal bipyramidal shape.

q: Among noble gases, xenon forms compounds with fluorine most readily because:
o: It has the lowest ionisation enthalpy among readily available noble gases
It has the smallest atomic size in the group
It is the most electronegative noble gas
It has no outer electrons at all
why: Reactivity increases down Group 18 as ionisation enthalpy decreases, making xenon (large, low IE) reactive enough to form compounds.
XeF4, formed from Xe + 2F2, has a square planar molecular shape.
